text:
maria: Heads-up — nightly fused-attn run shows a regression after the tiling + prefetch change. p50 up ~7%, p99 up ~18% for seq=1024 on A100. logs: ```gpu0: epilogue_time=1.92ms -> 2.10ms; total_step=6.3ms -> 6.9ms``` Anyone else see the same?

jonah: saw it, repro locally on devbox. Looks correlated with the new tiling stride (tile=64 -> 96). Might be causing worse L2 locality for epilogue.

kevin: can you paste the profiler flamegraph? curious whether the extra time is in the epilogue compute or memory stalls.

maria: pasted screenshot to thread (attached). quick perf counters: ```l2_hit_rate: 0.78 -> 0.64; dram_bw_util: 42% -> 56%``` so more DRAM pressure after tiling change.

sophia: that suggests prefetch distance/turnstile not tuned for the new tile width. We shifted qkv packing to aligned-vec stores which changes streaming patterns into epilogue. Prefetcher might be missing the window.

jonah: experiment idea: adaptive prefetcher that samples a few batches and picks prefetch distance per kernel per seq_len. Low overhead sampler: run 2 warmup iterations with both distances and pick the better one.

tyler: +1. we already have a cheap sampler in batch selection for kernel-chooser. reuse it: record p50 for short probe runs, cache choice for 30s. avoids expensive full benchmarks.

maria: did a quick run with sampler at seq=1024: chosen prefetch=32 for tile=96, p50 returned to baseline and p99 improved a bit. But we still see micro-regressions on page-aligned models (pagedKV): some workloads spike.

kevin: for pagedKV workloads, epilogue accesses are more irregular due to page fetches. Consider turning off epilogue fusion (split compute+write) when paged hits exceed threshold. Fusion helps when streaming is contiguous, hurts when you have a lot of random DRAM lookups.

sophia: agree. We can add a small heuristic: if kvcache_page_fault_rate > 0.02 for recent window or if l2_hit_rate < 0.7, fallback to split-epilogue. That should avoid worst-case thrash.

maria: implemented a PoC: sampler -> choose (tiled_kernel + prefetch) or (tiled_kernel + split-epilogue). On 20 runs it selected split-epilogue for pagedKV heavy profile and fused for dense. Overall tail dropped ~12% for pagedKV suite.

jonah: nice. do we need to expose this choice to runtime config? ops may want to pin behavior.

maria: yes, adding runtime toggle and an override env flag. default=auto. Will add metrics so console can show which branch served each request (model_id + kernel_choice tag).

perf-bot: CI perf check: fused-attn-tiling branch — summary: baseline delta p50 +1.1%, p99 +2.9% on aggregate. With sampler-enabled (opt-in) p50 -0.3%, p99 -1.2%. See CI artifact link: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/2387654321

tyler: next steps: 1) land sampler PoC behind feature flag, 2) add ephemeral caching of choices keyed by (model, seq_len, tile, pagedKV_flag), 3) add observability (per-route kernel tag), 4) run longer soak on Dedicated.

kevin: also add microbench for lane-starvation when tile changes. I saw an odd pattern where some SMs idle due to imbalance at tile=96 for heads=32. Could be a threadmapping issue.

maria: noted. I'll add a lane-utilization trace to the sampler probe so we capture that. Thanks folks — will open a PR with tests + perf artifacts.
